title: National Scholarship Portal SOP 2024
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

National Scholarship Portal — Standard Operating Procedure 2024

1. Eligibility
Scholarships under this scheme are open to Indian citizens who have completed Class 10 from a recognised board. Family income must not exceed INR 8 lakh per annum, supported by an income certificate issued by a competent revenue authority. The student must not be in receipt of any other central-government scholarship for the same course of study during the same academic year.

2. Application Process
All applications must be filed online through the National Scholarship Portal at scholarships.gov.in. The student must register with their Aadhaar number and a valid mobile number. After registration, fill in the personal details, academic details, and bank account details. Upload the scanned documents: income certificate, marksheet of the previous class, and bank passbook copy.

3. Verification
Institutions verify the application through their dedicated NSP login within 21 days of submission. If the institution fails to verify within 21 days, the application is marked for scrutiny by the State Nodal Officer. Scrutiny is completed within 30 days.

4. Disbursement
After scrutiny, scholarships are disbursed directly to the beneficiary bank account via DBT. The disbursement cycle is quarterly. Students can track the disbursement status on the portal using their application ID.

5. Appeals
If a scholarship is rejected, the student may file an appeal within 30 days of the rejection through the grievance redressal module of the portal. The appeal is reviewed by the Appellate Authority at the Ministry.

title: RTE Section 12(1)(c) Admission Circular
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

Circular: Implementation of Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act, 2009

Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act requires all specified-category schools and unaided private schools to reserve 25% of their entry-level seats for children from Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Disadvantaged Groups. Admission under this provision is at the entry level — Class 1 or pre-primary, as the case may be.

Application window: Applications open on 1 March and close on 31 March every year. Parents or guardians may submit the application online through the state's dedicated RTE portal or at the office of the District Education Officer.

Income criterion: The family income must not exceed INR 1 lakh per annum for the purpose of this provision. Income certificate must be issued by a competent authority and should not be older than 6 months at the time of application.

Age criterion: For Class 1, the child must be between 6 and 7 years of age as on 31 March of the admission year. For pre-primary, the age range is 3-6 years.

Lottery: Where the number of applications exceeds the seats available, admissions are made through a randomised lottery conducted in the presence of a District Magistrate nominee. The lottery is recorded on video. The list of selected candidates is published within 7 working days.

Reimbursement: The state government reimburses the school for the tuition fee of admitted children, capped at the per-child expenditure in the government school or the actual fee, whichever is lower. The reimbursement claim is filed by the school through the state RTE portal.

title: Mid-Day Meal Scheme FAQ
raw_text:
Frequently Asked Questions — PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal) Scheme

Q1. Who is eligible for the mid-day meal?
A1. All children studying in Classes 1 to 8 in government, government-aided, and local body schools are eligible. Children in Education Guarantee Society and Innovation centres run under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan are also covered.

Q2. What is the calorie norm per child per day?
A2. Primary classes (1-5): 450 kcal and 12g protein. Upper primary (6-8): 700 kcal and 20g protein. The meal is served hot, on every working day of the school.

Q3. What happens if the meal is not served?
A3. The school must report the gap to the Block Resource Coordinator. The cook-cum-helper must be paid for the working day regardless. Parents may file a grievance with the District Mid-Day Meal in-charge.

Q4. Can a cook be present without a health card?
A4. No. Every cook-cum-helper must undergo an annual health checkup and possess a valid health card. Children must not be served by anyone without a health card.

Q5. How are food grains supplied?
A5. Food grains (rice and wheat) are supplied by the Food Corporation of India at the rate of 100g per child per day for primary and 150g per child per day for upper primary. The grains are delivered to the school through the state-level nodal agency.

title: Teacher Transfer Policy
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

Teacher Transfer Policy — Annual Cycle

1. Transfer window: The annual transfer window opens on 1 May and closes on 15 June. All transfer requests must be filed online through the state's Human Resource Management System. No offline requests will be entertained.

2. Eligibility: A teacher must have completed at least 3 years of service at the current station to apply for transfer. For hardship postings in remote or Naxal-affected blocks, the minimum service is reduced to 2 years. Women teachers with a child below 5 years may request transfer to a station closer to their spouse's place of posting.

3. Grounds for transfer: Medical grounds (supported by a certificate from a district hospital), spouse grounds, and hardship grounds are the only valid grounds for out-of-turn transfer. The medical certificate must clearly state that the current station is adversely affecting the health of the teacher.

4. Transfer committee: The District Transfer Committee, headed by the District Education Officer, meets in the last week of June. The committee's decision is final and binding. The list of approved transfers is published on 30 June.

5. Appeal: A teacher aggrieved by the committee's decision may file an appeal with the Director of Public Instruction within 15 days of publication of the list. The appeal must specify the grounds on which the committee's decision is challenged.

title: NEP 2020 Implementation Note
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

National Education Policy 2020 — Implementation Note

This note outlines the operational framework for implementing the National Education Policy 2020, with specific guidance for state-level directorates.

1. 5+3+3+4 structure: The school education structure has been reorganised as 5 years of foundational stage, 3 years of preparatory, 3 years of middle, and 4 years of secondary. Foundational stage covers ages 3-8 and combines Anganwadi and Class 1-2. The preparatory stage (ages 8-11) covers Classes 3-5.

2. Mother-tongue instruction: Instruction in the foundational and preparatory stages will be in the mother tongue or local regional language wherever possible. The medium of instruction transitions to a second language from Class 6 onwards.

3. No hard separation: There is no rigid separation between arts, humanities, and sciences. Students will choose subjects across these streams in Classes 9-12.

4. Board examinations: Board examinations will be held twice a year, and a student may retain the better score. The examinations will test competencies, not rote memorisation.

5. Teacher training: All serving teachers must complete a 50-hour professional development programme annually. The training is delivered online through the NISHTHA portal.

title: Kendriya Vidyalaya Admission Guidelines
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan — Admission Guidelines 2024-25

1. Eligibility: Children of central-government employees, including defence personnel, are eligible for admission to Kendriya Vidyalayas. Children of state-government employees and self-employed persons are also eligible under separate quotas.

2. Application window: Online applications open on 1 April and close on 15 April for Class 1. For other classes, applications are accepted subject to seat availability.

3. Age: For Class 1, the child must be between 5 and 7 years of age as on 31 March of the admission year. There is a 2-year relaxation for children with disabilities.

4. Reservation: 15% seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes, 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes, and 27% for Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer). 3% of total seats are reserved for children with disabilities.

5. Priority categories: Admission is granted in priority order — central-government employees first, then PSU employees, then state-government employees, then others. Within each priority category, a lottery is conducted if seats are oversubscribed.

6. Special provisions: Children of martyred defence personnel, children of gallantry award winners, and children of Kargil war veterans are admitted out of turn over and above the regular seats.

title: Higher Education Scholarship for SC/ST Students
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

National Fellowship for Higher Education of SC/ST Students

1. Eligibility: SC and ST students who have secured admission to a full-time MPhil or PhD programme in a recognised university are eligible. The candidate must have cleared the UGC NET or the CSIR NET.

2. Fellowship amount: Junior Research Fellows receive INR 31,000 per month for the first two years and INR 35,000 per month for the third and subsequent years. A contingency grant of INR 10,000 per annum is also admissible.

3. Tenure: The fellowship is tenable for 5 years from the date of admission or completion of the PhD, whichever is earlier. The fellowship may be discontinued if the candidate fails to submit annual progress reports.

4. Leave: Fellows may avail up to 30 days of earned leave per year. Maternity leave of 180 days is admissible to women fellows as per the rules of the host institution.

5. Application: The application is filed online through the National Fellowship portal of the Ministry of Social Justice. The candidate must upload the NET certificate, marksheet of the previous degree, and a copy of the PhD admission letter.

title: SWAYAM Online Courses FAQ
raw_text:
Frequently Asked Questions — SWAYAM Online Courses

Q1. What is SWAYAM?
A1. SWAYAM is a programme initiated by the Government of India to provide free online courses to learners across India. Courses are offered by faculty from IITs, IIMs, central universities, and other recognised institutions.

Q2. Are the courses free?
A2. The course content is free. However, if a learner wants a certificate, a nominal examination fee of INR 1,000 per course is payable. The fee is waived for SC/ST candidates on submission of a certificate.

Q3. How do I register?
A3. Register at swayam.gov.in with your email and mobile number. Browse the catalogue, select a course, and click 'Enroll'. The course appears in your dashboard once the session begins.

Q4. What is the evaluation pattern?
A4. Each course has weekly assignments (carrying 25% weightage) and a proctored end-term examination (75% weightage). A learner must score at least 40% in the end-term exam to be eligible for a certificate.

Q5. Is the certificate valid?
A5. The certificate is recognised by the UGC for the purpose of credit transfer. The learner may transfer up to 20% of the total credits required for a degree through SWAYAM courses.

title: Anti-Ragging Cell Mandate
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

Anti-Ragging Cell Mandate — All Higher Education Institutions

1. Applicability: Every higher education institution in India must constitute an Anti-Ragging Cell. This includes central universities, state universities, deemed-to-be universities, private universities, and affiliated colleges.

2. Composition: The Cell shall be headed by the Head of the Institution. It must include the Dean of Students, two senior faculty members, a representative of the District Administration, and a student representative. The student representative is chosen by rotation each academic year.

3. Complaint mechanism: Any student may file a complaint of ragging in person, by email, or through the national anti-ragging helpline at 1800-180-5522. The identity of the complainant is kept confidential.

4. Investigation: The Cell must acknowledge the complaint within 24 hours and complete the inquiry within 7 days. If the inquiry is not completed within 7 days, the matter is referred to the District Anti-Ragging Committee.

5. Punishment: Punishments include suspension from classes, expulsion from the hostel, a fine of INR 25,000, and rustication from the institution. In cases of physical injury or sexual harassment, an FIR must be registered under the Indian Penal Code.

title: DIKSHA Educational Content Platform
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

DIKSHA — Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing

DIKSHA is the national digital platform for school education. It hosts curriculum-aligned e-content in 33 Indian languages, accessible to teachers, students, and parents across the country.

1. Content access: All content on DIKSHA is free. Teachers access it through the DIKSHA mobile app or the web portal at diksha.gov.in. Students and parents may also access the content via the same app.

2. QR-coded textbooks: State-board textbooks carry a QR code on each chapter. Scanning the code opens the relevant e-content on DIKSHA — videos, interactive quizzes, and additional reading material.

3. Teacher training: DIKSHA hosts the NISHTHA continuous professional development programme. Teachers complete 50 hours of online training per year, with a certificate issued on completion.

4. Content contribution: Teachers may contribute their own lesson plans, worksheets, and videos. Contributions are reviewed by a state-level curation team before publication.

5. Available languages: Content is available in Hindi, English, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu, among others.

title: PM-SHRI School Scheme
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

PM-SHRI Schools Scheme — Implementation Circular

1. Objective: The PM Schools for Rising India (PM-SHRI) scheme develops existing schools into model schools that exemplify the National Education Policy 2020. The scheme covers 14,500 schools over a 5-year period beginning 2022-23.

2. Selection of schools: Schools are selected through a challenge-mode competition. The selection criteria include infrastructure, learning outcomes, co-curricular activities, and the school's prior track record. State governments nominate schools; the central ministry makes the final selection.

3. Funding: The central government bears 60% of the project cost and the state government bears 40%. The funding is released in three tranches linked to milestones. The first tranche is released on selection; subsequent tranches are linked to the achievement of defined learning outcomes and infrastructure benchmarks.

4. Pedagogy: PM-SHRI schools follow experiential, inquiry-driven, and arts-integrated pedagogy. The medium of instruction in the foundational stage is the mother tongue. Every classroom is equipped with a digital board.

5. Assessment: PM-HRI schools follow the Holistic Progress Card for assessing students. The card captures academic progress, co-curricular performance, and 21st-century skills like collaboration and critical thinking.

title: Student Suicide Prevention Guidelines
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

Guidelines for Prevention of Student Suicides in Higher Educational Institutions

1. Counselling Cell: Every higher education institution must have a Counselling Cell with at least one trained counsellor per 1,000 students. The Cell is open during all working hours and offers confidential counselling to students in distress.

2. Buddy system: Each institution must implement a buddy system under which every first-year student is paired with a senior student. The buddy is responsible for reaching out to the buddy at least once a week and reporting any signs of distress.

3. Identification of warning signs: Warning signs include withdrawal from social contact, sudden drop in academic performance, talking about death, giving away prized possessions, and changes in sleeping or eating patterns. Faculty members must refer any student showing these signs to the Counselling Cell.

4. Helpline: The national helpline KIRAN for mental health support is accessible at 1800-599-0019. The helpline operates 24x7 and is available in 13 Indian languages.

5. Crisis response: In the event of a suicide attempt or completion, the institution must notify the parents immediately, the police within 2 hours, and the District Mental Health Programme coordinator. The institution must also offer post-trauma counselling to the deceased student's classmates and roommates.

title: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Implementation
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Education

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao — Implementation Note for District Magistrates

1. Objective: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education of the girl child. The scheme is implemented at the district level through the District Task Force.

2. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana: Under the scheme, parents of a girl child below 10 years may open a Sukanya Samriddhi Account at any post office or authorised bank. The minimum annual deposit is INR 250 and the maximum is INR 1.5 lakh. The account matures after 21 years from the date of opening or on the marriage of the girl, whichever is earlier.

3. Kanya Kelavani: The Kanya Kelavani drive is conducted in June every year to enrol out-of-school girls. The District Education Officer, the Taluka Development Officer, and the village Sarpanch jointly visit households and ensure enrolment.

4. District Magistrate's role: The DM chairs the District Task Force, which meets quarterly. The DM reviews the child sex ratio, the enrolment and retention of girls in schools, and the number of Sukanya Samriddhi accounts opened in the district.

5. Incentives: Girls who pass Class 10 with first class are eligible for an incentive of INR 5,000. The incentive is transferred directly to the girl's bank account via DBT.

title: Operation Greens — Tomato Onion Potato
raw_text:
Note: This circular is unrelated to education but is included here for testing.

Operation Greens is a price stabilisation scheme for tomato, onion, and potato (TOP) crops. The scheme provides a subsidy of 50% on transportation and storage of TOP crops from production to consumption centres. Farmers and Farmer Producer Organisations may apply through the NAFED portal.

title: Railway Ticket Refund Rules
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Passenger Ticket Refund Rules 2024

1. Cancellation before departure: If a confirmed ticket is cancelled more than 48 hours before the scheduled departure, the cancellation charge is INR 240 for AC First Class, INR 120 for AC 2 Tier, and INR 60 for AC 3 Tier and Sleeper. The remaining fare is refunded to the original payment instrument within 5-7 working days.

2. Cancellation within 48 hours: If a confirmed ticket is cancelled between 12 and 48 hours before departure, 25% of the fare is deducted as cancellation charge. If cancelled less than 12 hours but before departure, 50% is deducted.

3. Waitlist tickets: Waitlisted tickets automatically cancelled if not confirmed at the time of chart preparation are refunded in full without any deduction. The refund is processed within 3-5 working days.

4. Tatkal tickets: Tatkal ticket cancellation charges are higher. Confirmed Tatkal tickets cancelled up to 24 hours before departure attract 25% deduction. Within 24 hours, no refund is admissible except in case of train cancellation by the Railways.

5. TDR filing: For tickets where the passenger could not travel due to train delay of more than 3 hours, a TDR (Ticket Deposit Receipt) must be filed online within 72 hours of the scheduled departure. The refund is processed after verification by the commercial department.

title: Senior Citizen Concession Circular
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Concession to Senior Citizens — Revised Circular

1. Applicability: Senior citizens (men aged 60 years and above, women aged 58 years and above) are eligible for concession on fares in all classes of travel, subject to the conditions specified herein.

2. Concession rate: Men get 40% concession in AC classes and 50% in Sleeper and Second class. Women get 50% concession across all classes.

3. Verification: The concession is granted on production of a valid age proof — Aadhaar, Voter ID, driving licence, or passport. The age proof must be carried during the journey; failure to produce it on demand results in the concession being withdrawn and the differential fare being recovered with a penalty of INR 250.

4. Tatkal bookings: The concession is not admissible on Tatkal quota. Senior citizens booking Tatkal tickets pay the full Tatkal fare.

5. Combined with other concessions: Senior citizen concession cannot be combined with any other concession except the cancer patient concession, which is governed by a separate circular.

title: Railway Grievance Redressal Mechanism
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Grievance Redressal Mechanism for Passengers

1. Filing a grievance: A passenger may file a grievance through the CPGRAMS portal at pgportal.gov.in, the Rail Madad portal, the SMS service at 139, the X (formerly Twitter) handle of the Railway Ministry, or by writing to the General Manager of the concerned Zonal Railway.

2. Time limits: A grievance relating to cleanliness, catering, or staff behaviour must be acknowledged within 24 hours and redressed within 7 days. A grievance relating to refund of fare or compensation for loss of baggage must be redressed within 30 days.

3. Appeal: If the passenger is not satisfied with the redressal, an appeal may be filed with the Appellate Authority within 30 days of the redressal. The Appellate Authority is the Additional General Manager of the Zonal Railway concerned.

4. Compensation: Compensation up to INR 1 lakh may be awarded for deficient service, on the recommendation of the Appellate Authority. The compensation is sanctioned by the General Manager and disbursed through NEFT.

5. Helpline: The all-India helpline 139 is available 24x7 in 12 Indian languages. Passengers may also approach the Superintendent of the station directly for on-the-spot redressal of routine matters like bedding, catering, or coach cleanliness.

title: Railway Land Licensing Policy
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Land Licensing Policy for Commercial Use of Railway Land

1. Applicability: This policy governs the licensing of railway land to private parties for commercial, institutional, or industrial use. The licensing is for a fixed tenure and the land continues to be owned by the Railways.

2. Tenure: The minimum licensing tenure is 5 years and the maximum is 35 years. The licence is renewable at the discretion of the Railways, subject to satisfactory performance of the licensee.

3. Eligibility: Any Indian company, partnership firm, or society registered under the Societies Registration Act may apply. The applicant must have a net worth of at least INR 1 crore and should not be in default of any dues to the Railways or the Government.

4. Process: Applications are invited through open tender on the Indian Railway e-procurement portal. The licence fee is determined through a transparent bidding process. The highest bidder is selected, subject to meeting the eligibility criteria.

5. Termination: The licence may be terminated by the Railways on breach of any term, with a 90-day notice. The licensee must vacate the land and remove all structures within 6 months of termination. The security deposit is forfeited in case of non-compliance.

title: Railway Station Redevelopment FAQ
raw_text:
Frequently Asked Questions — Station Redevelopment Programme

Q1. What is the Station Redevelopment Programme?
A1. The programme aims to redevelop major railway stations across India with modern passenger amenities, world-class architecture, and integrated multi-modal connectivity. The programme covers 1,300 stations across the country over a 5-year period.

Q2. How is it being funded?
A2. The programme is being implemented through the Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) model and the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. The funding is a mix of railway budgetary support, internal extra-budgetary resources, and PPP investments.

Q3. What amenities are being added?
A3. Each redeveloped station will have a spacious waiting hall, lift and escalator access to all platforms, integrated signages in 3 languages, dedicated spaces for divyangjan passengers, retail and food courts, and a roof plaza for community gatherings.

Q4. Will train operations continue during redevelopment?
A4. Yes. Redevelopment is carried out in phases to ensure minimal disruption to train operations. Temporary passenger amenities are provided during the construction period.

Q5. How can I give feedback on a redeveloped station?
A5. Passengers may give feedback through the Rail Madad portal, the 139 helpline, or the suggestion box at the station. Feedback is reviewed by the Station Director and acted upon within 7 days.

title: Vande Bharat Train Maintenance SOP
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Vande Bharat Express — Maintenance Standard Operating Procedure

1. Daily inspection: Each Vande Bharat rake undergoes a daily inspection at the base maintenance depot. The inspection covers the brake system, the coupler, the door system, the air-conditioning, and the passenger information system. The inspection takes approximately 4 hours and is conducted overnight.

2. Periodic overhauls: A 12-day periodic overhaul is conducted every 4 months. The overhaul involves the inspection of the bogie, the traction motor, the auxiliary transformer, and the battery bank. The roof-mounted air-conditioning units are dismantled and cleaned.

3. Annual overhaul: The annual overhaul is conducted every 18 months. The coach is lifted off the bogies, the bogies are stripped down to the bare frame, and all components are inspected for cracks, wear, and corrosion. The wheels are reprofiled on a wheel lathe.

4. Cleaning: External cleaning of the rake is done daily at the base depot using a mechanised coach washing plant. Internal cleaning — including bio-vacuum toilet cleaning — is done at the end of every trip. The coach interior is sanitised using food-safe disinfectants.

5. Spare parts: Critical spare parts are stocked at the base depot. The inventory is monitored through the Integrated Coaching Stock Management System. A spare-parts consignment is replenished weekly based on consumption.

title: Railway Recruitment Process
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Railway Recruitment — Standard Operating Procedure

1. Notification: All recruitment to Group C and Group D posts is notified through the Employment News and the official websites of the Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs). The notification specifies the number of vacancies, eligibility, examination pattern, and the application deadline.

2. Application: Applications are accepted only online through the RRB portal. The application fee is INR 500 for general and OBC candidates and INR 250 for SC, ST, women, and PwD candidates. The fee for SC, ST, women, Ex-servicemen, and PwD candidates is refunded on appearing for the first stage of the examination.

3. Examination: Most recruitments involve a Computer Based Test (CBT) of 90 minutes. The CBT has 100 questions covering General Awareness, Arithmetic, General Intelligence, and Reasoning. There is a negative marking of 1/3 for each wrong answer.

4. Result and allotment: Candidates qualifying in the CBT appear for a skill test (wherever applicable) and a document verification. The merit list is prepared on the basis of CBT marks. Allotment of post and zone is based on the candidate's rank and preference.

5. Medical examination: Candidates are subjected to a medical examination by the Railway Medical Authority before appointment. The medical standards vary by post — A1, A2, B1, B2, C, and C1. Failure to meet the medical standard results in disqualification.

title: Freight Corridor Operations
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Dedicated Freight Corridor — Operations Circular

1. Overview: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) operates the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors. The corridors are exclusively for freight trains and are not open to passenger traffic.

2. Freight rates: The freight rates on the DFC are distance-based and vary by commodity. The rate for container traffic is INR 1.40 per tonne-km. The rate for coal is INR 1.10 per tonne-km. Rates are reviewed quarterly by a tariff committee.

3. Train length: Freight trains on the DFC may be up to 1.5 km long, with a maximum payload of 13,000 tonnes. The standard block rake is 58 BOXN wagons with a payload of approximately 3,500 tonnes.

4. Speed: Freight trains on the DFC operate at a maximum speed of 100 kmph. The average end-to-end speed, including halts, is 50 kmph. The DFC is designed to reduce the Mumbai-Delhi transit time from 36 hours to 24 hours.

5. Customer interface: Customers may track their consignments through the FOIS (Freight Operations Information System) portal. The portal provides real-time status of wagon placement, loading, in-transit movement, and unloading at the destination.

title: Railway Pension Disbursement
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Pension Disbursement SOP for Retired Railway Employees

1. Pension sanction: The pension is sanctioned by the competent authority (usually the Divisional Railway Manager) on the basis of the service book of the employee. The service book is verified by the Accounts Department and the pension is calculated as per the rules in force on the date of retirement.

2. Commutation: A railway employee may commute up to 40% of the pension. The commuted value is paid as a lump sum on retirement. The commuted portion of the pension is restored after 15 years from the date of retirement.

3. Disbursement: The pension is disbursed through the State Bank of India, public sector banks, or post offices. The pensioner must submit a life certificate every November. Pensioners above 80 years may submit the certificate any time after 1 November.

4. Family pension: On the death of the pensioner, the family pension is admissible to the spouse. The family pension is 30% of the last pay drawn for those retired before 1 January 2006 and 50% for those retired on or after that date.

5. Medical: The pensioner is eligible for medical facilities under the RELHS (Railway Employees Liberalised Health Scheme). The RELHS card is issued by the Personnel Branch of the parent division and is valid for life.

title: Suburban Railway Network Expansion
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Suburban Railway Expansion Plan — Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata

1. Mumbai suburban: The Mumbai suburban network is being expanded with the addition of two new corridors — the Virar-Dahanu corridor and the Panvel-Karjat corridor. The new corridors will be operated by the Central Railway and will be integrated with the existing Mumbai suburban network.

2. Chennai suburban: The Chennai suburban network is being expanded with the addition of a fourth line between Chennai Beach and Tambaram. The fourth line will increase the line capacity from 26 trains per hour to 40 trains per hour.

3. Kolkata suburban: The Kolkata suburban network is being modernised with the introduction of air-conditioned local trains. The AC locals operate on the Sealdah-Hasnabad and Howrah-Shiroman routes.

4. Fares: Suburban fares are structured as distance-based slabs. The minimum fare is INR 5 and the maximum is INR 50. A monthly season ticket is available at approximately 15 times the one-way fare.

5. Crowding: Suburban trains in Mumbai operate at over 4,500 passengers per 9-car rake against a capacity of 1,700. The expansion plan aims to reduce the load to 3,500 passengers per rake by 2027.

title: Accident Compensation Rules
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Railway Accident Compensation Rules

1. Definition: An 'accident' for the purpose of these rules includes collision, derailment, fire, explosion, or any other unusual event resulting in injury or loss of life to passengers. The rules apply to accidents occurring in railway premises including platforms, foot overbridges, and running trains.

2. Compensation for death: In case of death of a passenger, the compensation payable is INR 8 lakh. The compensation is paid by the Railway Claims Tribunal (RCT) on the basis of an inquiry report.

3. Compensation for injury: For loss of a limb or functional impairment, the compensation ranges from INR 64,000 to INR 4 lakh depending on the extent of the disability. For minor injuries requiring hospitalisation up to 7 days, the compensation is INR 25,000.

4. Claim procedure: The claim is filed before the RCT having jurisdiction over the place of accident. The claim application must be accompanied by the ticket, the FIR, the medical report, and the death certificate (in case of death). The claim must be filed within one year of the accident.

5. Ex-gratia: In addition to the compensation, an ex-gratia payment is made by the General Manager of the Zonal Railway. The ex-gratia is INR 5 lakh for death, INR 1 lakh for grievous injury, and INR 15,000 for simple injury. The ex-gratia is paid within 24 hours of the accident.

title: Railway Catering Policy
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Catering Policy 2024 — Pantry Car and Stall Operations

1. Pantry cars: Pantry cars are attached to long-distance mail and express trains with a journey time of more than 12 hours. The pantry car serves breakfast, lunch, evening snacks, and dinner. The menu is fixed by the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC).

2. Menu rates: The menu rates are notified by the IRCTC and are uniform across all trains. A vegetarian thali is priced at INR 120, a non-vegetarian thali at INR 160, and a morning tea with two biscuits at INR 20. The menu is displayed in every coach.

3. Quality control: Random inspections are conducted by the IRCTC quality cell and the Railway's commercial department. Samples of food items are sent to NABL-accredited laboratories for testing. Deficiencies are recorded and the caterer is fined as per the contract.

4. Stall licensing: Food stalls at railway stations are licensed by the Zonal Railway through open tender. The licence is for 5 years and is renewable. The licensee must comply with the FSSAI regulations and maintain hygiene standards.

5. Complaint mechanism: A passenger may complain about catering through the Rail Madad portal, the 139 helpline, or directly to the Pantry Car Manager. The complaint must be acknowledged within 24 hours and redressed within 7 days.

title: Tourist Train Operations
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Tourist Train Operations — Bharat Gaurav Scheme

1. Scheme: The Bharat Gaurav Tourist Train scheme operates tourist trains on identified circuits. The trains are owned by the Railways but are operated by registered tour operators. The scheme covers 12 circuits including the Ramayana Circuit, the Buddhist Circuit, and the North East Circuit.

2. Booking: The tour operator books the entire train for a fixed tenure — typically 7 to 14 days. The operator designs the itinerary including the tourist spots, the hotels, and the meals. The Railways provide the rake, the crew, the maintenance, and the running rights.

3. Composition: Each tourist train has 14 coaches — 4 AC 1 Tier, 5 AC 2 Tier, 2 AC 3 Tier, 1 Pantry Car, and 2 Generator-cum-Luggage vans. The train can accommodate approximately 150 tourists.

4. Stops: The train stops at identified tourist stations for sightseeing. The halt duration is typically 6 hours at major stations and 3 hours at minor stations. The tour operator arranges local transportation for the tourists during the halt.

5. Pricing: The tour operator fixes the per-passenger rate based on the train composition, the tenure, and the itinerary. The Railways' revenue is the lease charge for the rake and is independent of the operator's pricing.

title: Railway Signal Modernisation
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Signal Modernisation Programme — Implementation Note

1. Objective: The signal modernisation programme aims to replace over 1,200 relay-based interlocking systems with electronic interlocking over a 5-year period. The programme also introduces the European Train Control System (ETCS) Level 2 across 5,000 route km.

2. Electronic interlocking: Electronic interlocking (EI) replaces the bulky relay rooms with microprocessor-based interlocking. EI has a smaller footprint, is easier to maintain, and supports advanced features like automatic route setting and automatic block signalling.

3. ETCS Level 2: ETCS Level 2 is a train-protection system that supervises train movement on a continuous basis. The system receives movement authority from the Radio Block Centre (RBC) over a GSM-R radio link. The system applies brakes automatically if the train exceeds the permitted speed.

4. Implementation: The programme is being implemented through the Indian Railway's signalling works organisation. The contracts are awarded through open tender on the Indian Railway e-procurement portal. The major vendors include Medha, Kernex, and Hitachi.

5. Training: Signal maintenance personnel are trained at the Indian Railway Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications (IRISET) at Secunderabad. The training covers EI maintenance, ETCS Level 2 operations, and GSM-R radio troubleshooting.

title: Railway Passenger Insurance Scheme
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Railways

Optional Travel Insurance for Reserved Passengers

1. Applicability: Optional travel insurance is available to all passengers holding a confirmed or RAC ticket booked through the IRCTC portal. The scheme is not applicable to suburban or unreserved passengers.

2. Premium: The premium is INR 0.45 per passenger per journey. The premium is collected at the time of booking the ticket and is included in the fare. The passenger is auto-enrolled unless they explicitly opt out at the time of booking.

3. Coverage: The insurance covers death due to train accident (INR 10 lakh), permanent disability (INR 10 lakh), injury (INR 2 lakh), and loss of belongings (INR 40,000). The coverage is valid from the time of boarding until the time of alighting at the destination.

4. Claim process: In the event of an accident, the claim is filed with the insurance company through the IRCTC portal. The claim must be accompanied by the ticket, the FIR, the medical report, and the bank account details. The claim is settled within 30 days.

5. Helpline: A dedicated 24x7 helpline at 139 is available for insurance-related queries. The helpline also connects the passenger to the insurance company's representative in case of an emergency.

title: Ayushman Bharat PMJAY Implementation
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Ayushman Bharat PMJAY — Implementation Circular for State Health Agencies

1. Eligibility: Families identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 database are eligible. The eligibility is based on deprivation and occupational criteria. The family is identified by the Aadhaar of the head of the family.

2. Coverage: Each eligible family is entitled to INR 5 lakh of health insurance coverage per year. The coverage includes hospitalisation, surgery, and follow-up treatment. Pre-existing conditions are covered from day one — there is no waiting period.

3. Empanelment: Hospitals are empanelled by the State Health Agency (SHA). The empanelment criteria include infrastructure, manpower, and equipment. The hospital must be NABH-accredited (or NABL-accredited for diagnostics) for empanelment at higher-tier packages.

4. Claim process: The claim is filed by the hospital through the IT platform of the National Health Authority. The claim is pre-authorised before the procedure is undertaken. Post-procedure, the claim is submitted within 48 hours of discharge. The claim is settled within 15 days of submission.

5. Portability: A beneficiary can avail treatment at any empanelled hospital across India. The portability is built into the IT platform — the beneficiary is identified by the Aadhaar or the PMJAY ID card at the hospital.

title: Universal Immunisation Programme
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) — Vaccination Schedule

1. BCG: Bacille Calmette-Guérin vaccine against tuberculosis. Given at birth or within the first 2 weeks. Route: intradermal. Dose: 0.05 ml (under 1 year), 0.1 ml (1 year and above).

2. OPV: Oral Polio Vaccine. Five doses — at birth (zero dose), and at 6, 10, 14 weeks, and 9 months. The birth dose is critical for the induction of mucosal immunity. Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) is given intramuscularly at 6 and 14 weeks.

3. Pentavalent: A combination vaccine against Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b. Given at 6, 10, and 14 weeks. Route: intramuscular, anterolateral thigh.

4. Measles-Rubella (MR): Given at 9 months and 18 months. The MR campaign covers children between 9 months and 15 years for the elimination of measles and rubella.

5. Adverse Events Following Immunisation (AEFI): All AEFIs must be reported within 24 hours. Severe AEFIs are investigated by the District AEFI Committee within 7 days. The report is forwarded to the National AEFI Secretariat.

title: PM National Dialysis Programme
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP)

1. Objective: The PMNDP provides free dialysis to Below Poverty Line (BPL) patients and subsidised dialysis to others, in all district hospitals across India. The scheme is being implemented through a PPP mode with the private partner providing dialysis machines, technicians, and consumables.

2. Eligibility: BPL patients are eligible for free dialysis. Other patients may avail dialysis at a subsidised rate of INR 100 per session (the actual cost is approximately INR 2,000 per session).

3. Capacity: Each district hospital is equipped with 10-15 dialysis machines. The capacity is enhanced based on the demand. The dialysis is provided in two shifts — morning and afternoon.

4. Referral: Patients are referred to the district hospital by the Primary Health Centre or by a private nephrologist. The referral must specify the diagnosis, the modality of dialysis (haemodialysis or peritoneal), and the frequency.

5. Quality: The dialysis machines are equipped with online haemodiafiltration facility. The water treatment plant uses reverse osmosis. The consumables are single-use and disposed of as per biomedical waste rules.

title: Vector Borne Disease Control
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme — Malaria, Dengue, Chikungunya

1. Surveillance: Each Primary Health Centre and Community Health Centre reports the number of fever cases and confirmed vector-borne disease cases through the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) on a weekly basis.

2. Diagnosis: Malaria is diagnosed by either microscopy (blood slide examination) or by Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT). Dengue and chikungunya are diagnosed by ELISA tests conducted at district-level laboratories.

3. Treatment: Uncomplicated malaria is treated with Artemisinin Combination Therapy (ACT) — artesunate + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. Severe malaria is treated with injectable artesunate. Dengue has no specific antiviral treatment; management is symptomatic with paracetamol and fluids.

4. Vector control: Indoor residual spraying (IRS) with synthetic pyrethroids is conducted in high-risk villages. Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs) are distributed in tribal areas with high malaria prevalence. Source reduction — removal of stagnant water — is the primary dengue control strategy.

5. Outbreak response: An outbreak is defined as a doubling of cases in a week compared to the previous week. The district Rapid Response Team is activated within 24 hours. The team conducts active case finding, fever surveys, and entomological surveillance. Additional vector control measures including fogging are undertaken.

title: TB Elimination Programme
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) — Operational Guidelines

1. Goal: India aims to eliminate TB by 2025, five years ahead of the global SDG target. Elimination is defined as an incidence of less than 10 cases per 1,00,000 population.

2. Diagnosis: Sputum microscopy is the primary diagnostic modality. The Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (CBNAAT) — branded as GeneXpert — is used for drug-resistant TB diagnosis. TrueNAT is used at the peripheral level for screening.

3. Treatment: Drug-sensitive TB is treated with a fixed-dose combination of four drugs — Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, and Ethambutol — for 6 months. Drug-resistant TB is treated with a longer regimen of 9-12 months or a shorter regimen of 4-6 months with bedaquiline.

4. Nikshay: The Nikshay portal is the single window for case notification, treatment adherence tracking, and DBT of the patient support (Nikshay Poshan Yojana) of INR 500 per month. The portal is also used for the TB Mukt Bharat donor-patient (Nikshay Mitra) scheme.

5. TB Mukt Bharat: A community-led initiative where individuals, corporates, and NGOs adopt TB patients and provide nutritional, diagnostic, and vocational support. The adoption is for the full duration of treatment — typically 6 months for drug-sensitive TB.

title: Jan Aushadhi Scheme FAQ
raw_text:
Frequently Asked Questions — Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)

Q1. What is the Janaushadhi Scheme?
A1. PMBJP provides quality medicines at affordable prices through Janaushadhi Kendras. The medicines are generic equivalents of branded drugs and are priced 50-90% lower than the branded versions.

Q2. Where can I find a Janaushadhi Kendra?
A2. Janaushadhi Kendras are located at district headquarters, taluka headquarters, and at major railway stations. There are over 9,000 kendras across India. The kendras can be located on the Janaushadhi mobile app.

Q3. Do I need a prescription to buy medicines?
A3. For schedule H drugs (antibiotics, anti-tubercular, anti-diabetic), a prescription is mandatory. For over-the-counter medicines (paracetamol, ORS, antacid), no prescription is needed.

Q4. Are the medicines of the same quality as branded ones?
A4. Yes. The medicines are manufactured in WHO-GMP certified facilities. Each batch is tested by the Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India (BPPI) before distribution.

Q5. What is the pricing?
A5. The ceiling price is fixed by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) under the Drug Price Control Order. The Janaushadhi version is typically 50% of the ceiling price.

title: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Telemedicine Practice Guidelines 2024 — for Registered Medical Practitioners

1. Eligibility: Only Registered Medical Practitioners (RMPs) enrolled in the Indian Medical Register or a State Medical Register are permitted to practise telemedicine. The RMP must have a valid RMP ID issued by the National Medical Commission.

2. Modalities: Telemedicine consultation may be conducted through video, audio, or text (WhatsApp, email, or specialised app). The RMP must use a secure and encrypted platform. The consultation is recorded in the patient's medical record.

3. Medicines: Medicines may be prescribed based on the consultation. The list of medicines that can be prescribed via telemedicine is restricted — Schedule X drugs (e.g., psychotropics) and narcotics are excluded.

4. First consultation: In the first consultation, the RMP must verify the patient's identity by photo ID. If the patient is a minor, the parent or guardian must be present. The RMP must take a detailed medical history including allergies, current medications, and past illnesses.

5. Follow-up: Follow-up consultations may be conducted via audio alone. The RMP must document the response to treatment, any adverse events, and the next steps. The prescription is sent to the patient electronically with the RMP's signature and RMP ID.

title: Mental Healthcare Act Implementation
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Mental Healthcare Act 2017 — Implementation Note for State Mental Health Authorities

1. Rights of persons with mental illness: Every person with mental illness has the right to access mental healthcare and treatment from mental health services run or funded by the government. The person has the right to live in, be part of, and not be segregated from, society.

2. Advance Directive: A person may make an Advance Directive specifying the treatment they wish to receive or not receive in case they become unable to make decisions. The Directive is registered with the State Mental Health Board and is binding on the medical professional.

3. Nominated Representative: A person may nominate a representative to take decisions on their behalf if they lose capacity. The nominated representative is registered with the Mental Health Board.

4. Informed consent: All treatment requires informed consent except in emergencies. For electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), additional safeguards apply — ECT is prohibited on minors except in exceptional circumstances and never as a form of punishment.

5. Decriminalisation of suicide: Suicide attempts are decriminalised. A person who attempts suicide is presumed to be under severe stress and is entitled to treatment and support from the government.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Institutional Delivery Incentive Scheme

1. Eligibility: All pregnant women from Below Poverty Line (BPL) households are eligible. In the low-performing states (Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP, Odisha, Rajasthan, UP, Uttarakhand), all pregnant women are eligible regardless of BPL status.

2. Incentive: In high-performing states, the incentive is INR 1,400 for rural and INR 1,000 for urban. In low-performing states, the incentive is INR 1,400 for both. The ASHA worker assisting the delivery receives INR 600 in rural and INR 400 in urban areas.

3. Disbursement: The incentive is paid directly to the beneficiary's bank account via DBT within 7 days of the delivery. The ASHA's incentive is paid separately.

4. Eligibility criteria: The woman must be 19 years or above. The woman must have a mother-baby protection card. The delivery must have occurred in a government health facility or an accredited private hospital.

5. Reporting: Every delivery under JSY must be reported on the Health Management Information System (HMIS) portal within 7 days. The State Health Society conducts a quarterly verification of 10% of the reported deliveries.

title: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) — Child Health Screening

1. Objective: RBSK aims at early identification and early intervention for children from birth to 18 years with defects at birth, deficiencies, diseases, and developmental delays. The programme covers 30 selected health conditions.

2. Screening teams: Each block has two Mobile Health Teams. Each team has a Medical Officer (AYUSH), an ANM, and a pharmacist. The teams visit Anganwadi centres and government schools on a fixed schedule — typically once in 6 months.

3. Defects covered: The defects screened include congenital cataract, congenital deafness, cleft lip and palate, clubfoot, developmental dysplasia of the hip, and congenital heart disease.

4. Referral: Children identified with any of the 30 conditions are referred to the District Early Intervention Centre (DEIC). The DEIC has a team of specialists including a paediatrician, an ophthalmologist, an ENT specialist, an orthopaedic surgeon, and a physiotherapist.

5. Surgery: Surgeries are conducted at tertiary-level facilities — medical colleges or regional hospitals. The cost of surgery is borne under the Rashtriya Bal Kalyan Kosh (RBKK). The follow-up is coordinated by the DEIC.

title: COVID-19 Vaccination Booster Policy
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

COVID-19 Precautionary (Booster) Dose Policy 2024

1. Applicability: The precautionary dose is available to all adults aged 18 years and above. The dose is administered free of cost at government vaccination centres. The dose is also available at private centres on payment.

2. Interval: The precautionary dose is administered 6 months (26 weeks) after the second dose. For immunocompromised individuals, the interval may be reduced to 3 months on the advice of the treating physician.

3. Choice of vaccine: The beneficiary may choose the same vaccine as the primary series (homologous boosting) or a different vaccine (heterologous boosting). The heterologous boosting is recommended by the National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) based on emerging evidence.

4. Registration: Registration is voluntary. The beneficiary may walk in to any government vaccination centre without prior appointment. The CoWIN portal generates the digital certificate within 24 hours.

5. Reporting: All adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) are reported through the CoWIN portal. Severe AEFIs are investigated by the district AEFI committee within 7 days. The report is forwarded to the National AEFI Secretariat.

title: National Leprosy Eradication Programme
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) — Operational Guidelines

1. Goal: The NLEP aims to eliminate leprosy as a public health problem (defined as a prevalence of less than 1 case per 10,000 population). India achieved elimination at the national level in 2005 but high-burden districts remain.

2. Diagnosis: Leprosy is diagnosed clinically based on skin lesions and peripheral nerve involvement. There is no routine serological test. Slit skin smear is used in selected cases for confirmation and for classifying into paucibacillary (PB) and multibacillary (MB).

3. Treatment: Multidrug Therapy (MDT) is the standard treatment. PB leprosy is treated with 6 doses of rifampicin + dapsone over 6 months. MB leprosy is treated with 12 doses of rifampicin + clofazimine + dapsone over 12 months. The medicines are supplied in blister packs free of cost.

4. Disability prevention: Patients with nerve function impairment are referred to the district disability prevention and medical rehabilitation (DPMR) cell. The cell provides physiotherapy, self-care training, and surgical correction of deformities.

5. Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign (SLAC): A community-based campaign conducted in high-burden districts to promote early case detection and to reduce stigma. The campaign is conducted through village-level meetings and school-based awareness programmes.

title: National Mental Health Helpline KIRAN
raw_text:
Government of India
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

KIRAN — National Mental Health Helpline

1. Contact: The KIRAN helpline is accessible at 1800-599-0019. The helpline is operational 24x7. The call is free from all mobile and landline numbers in India.

2. Languages: The helpline is available in 13 Indian languages — Assamese, Bengali, English, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu. The caller is connected to a counsellor in the chosen language.

3. Services: The helpline provides first-line counselling, emotional support, and referral to district mental health programmes. The counsellors are trained psychologists and clinical psychologists. The helpline is supervised by the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS).

4. Confidentiality: All conversations are confidential. The counsellor does not record the identity of the caller. In cases of imminent risk of suicide, the counsellor may, with the caller's consent, refer to the district mental health cell for in-person follow-up.

5. Caller demographics: The helpline receives approximately 10,000 calls per month. The callers are predominantly in the 18-35 age group. The most common reasons for calling are academic stress, relationship issues, workplace stress, and pre-existing mental health conditions.
